summary.headline: Prasol Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR413 crore (+38.6% YoY) and EBITDA INR58 crore (+86.1%), with FY27 guidance reiterated.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR413 crore, up 38.6% YoY, driven mainly by higher realisations with single-digit domestic volume growth. EBITDA rose 86.1% to INR58 crore and PAT rose 122.2% to INR38 crore. H1 FY27 EBITDA of INR148 crore included a one-time INR25 crore inventory gain and INR0.92 crore forex gain in Q1, and management said underlying full-year EBITDA should be INR240-250 crore. Working capital cycle lengthened from 63 to 76 days as the company added shorter-credit suppliers, and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

financial_highlights.change: +106% YoY; includes INR25 crore inventory gain and INR0.92 crore forex gain in Q1
up from 63 days at end Q1 FY27

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Q2 growth was driven by higher realisations, with single-digit volume growth in the domestic business.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Agro is about 15-16% of top line per analyst; October agro sales grew 150%. One molecule (7-8% of agro products) has only two Indian manufacturers. Management said no further agro investment is planned.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 25% of revenue, held back by freight (sea freight up 2.5-3x to US and 7-8x on some routes). Target is 30%+ of revenue. Gross contribution is 30-35%, with manufacturing around 35% and distribution around 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR1,550-1,650 crore; EBITDA INR240-250 crore, excluding geopolitical price gains and forex, implying about 70-75% EBITDA growth YoY.
Management said profit before tax for H1 has already exceeded last year's full-year PAT base; H1 EBITDA and PAT already exceed last year's H1 figures.
Working capital cycle expected to return to the normal 60-70 day range; management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 FY27.
Long-term scale target of INR2,800-3,000 crore revenue in about 5 years. Management declined to share a 5-year EBITDA margin target.
FY28 guidance not given; management said it is too early to discuss.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 capex INR250-300 crore: about INR75 crore spent so far (H1 FY27 spend about INR75 crore); INR75-100 crore more planned before year-end.
Phase 1 adds about 60,000 tonnes, taking installed capacity to 150,000-160,000 tonnes over 12-24 months; about 25% of projects to go live by June-July 2027 and another 25% in H2 FY28.
Mechanical completion targeted by March 2027; about 3 months from mechanical completion to commercial production after sample approval.
Phase 2 capex INR250-300 crore for R&D-led products (mining chemicals, lubricants, pharma); propylene-based project needs about 2.5 years (CCOE and land approvals), the other about 1.5-2 years.
Additional domestic acetone capacity expected from January 2027; planned Khopoli storage facility for bulk procurement.
Antibacterial drug new process needs 3-6 months of requalification; lubricant additive capacity is a volume ramp-up, with the company sold out on current output.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from domestic and international customers remains healthy, the order book is strong, and the last month had the highest sales ever.
Raw material prices remain elevated; the company has added suppliers and customers across geographies. Shipping times for some inputs rose from 1-1.5 months to about 4 months.
Pricing pass-through: price increases pass to customers after 10-15 days; price cuts are passed on with a 15-30 day lag. Top 10 customers are on a formula-based supply arrangement.

Mining chemicals: a US lab approval was received; the company is now in mine-wise trials (South Africa and others), moving to bidding once mine approvals come. Management expects a breakthrough within about 2.5 years, possibly sooner.
Phosphorus-based products have about 2-2.5 months of visibility and are fully sold out.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY28 look for sales and EBITDA, and what new products and applications will come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers, citing the geopolitical situation. Expansions are in existing products already approved by end customers. Lubricant additives are in volume ramp-up and fully sold; antibacterial drug re-approval takes 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of inventory loss if crude corrects, and how is it mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a formula-based pricing arrangement with its top 10 customers and books inventory only against order visibility. Price cuts are passed on with a 15-30 day lag, so the company is exposed when prices fall and benefits when they rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow negative, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H1 cash flow is a snapshot and the working capital build reflects new suppliers, higher inventory cost and longer shipping times. Management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 and expects to rebuild inventory in Q4 if demand holds.

qa_highlights.question: What are plant utilisation levels and which industries are targeted by expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined utilisation of both plants is about 65-75%. Expansions cover every non-agro product, with increases of 30-100%. Forward integration and identical plants for lubricant grades are planned.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Q2 growth came from volume?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth came from higher realisations, with single-digit volume growth in the domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of renewable power at Mahad?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is laying an own cable from the grid (INR2.5-3 crore, due in 1.5-2 months). Current Mahad power costs INR9-9.5 per unit, with expected savings of INR1.25-1.50 per unit subject to solar regulations.

risks_watch: Working capital cycle at 76 days versus the 60-70 day target; H1 operating cash flow was negative.
Inventory valuation risk if crude and derivative prices fall; the pass-through lag is 15-30 days.
Phase 1 commissioning in stages (June-July 2027 and H2 FY28); execution and cost overrun risk on capex.
Export share at about 25% versus 30%+ target, dependent on freight normalisation.
Dependence on a few manufacturers in key molecules; the H1 earnings base includes a one-time INR25 crore gain.
Long-term INR2,800-3,000 crore revenue target relies on Phase 2 and R&D products that take 1.5-2.5 years to build.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q2 results and reiterated FY27 guidance, with several claims of record performance. Cautious and deliberately vague on FY28 and the 5-year EBITDA margin, citing geopolitical uncertainty. Management repeatedly stressed that the Q1 INR25 crore inventory gain is excluded from underlying EBITDA.
key_quotes: I am very happy to announce that this has been one of our best Q2 of Prasol ever.
We are extremely well placed and we have seen every time in crisis, when crisis comes, we end up doing better generally.
So we are light on agro. Whatever we have invested is what we are going to reap. We are not investing any further into that.
We are not here to make a short-term gain on you.
